chapter: Bands and musicians around New Orleans
title: Excursion dates at Bay St. Louis, Mandeville and river towns
summary: Weekend work across the lake and in Lake Charles, Shreveport and Lafayette; Bunk Johnson and John Handy come up.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you spend much time over around Bay St. Louis and past Christiana?

No, just on Sundays, you know. We'd go over there just for people we know, you know. Yeah. Just go over there and have a good time. Oh, but I played, you know. But the band, Lori, we played over past Christiana.
Did you know the Handy family and past Christiana? John Handy?
John Handy? Yeah. Oh, yeah.
Senior, I'm talking about. Had all the sons that played. I know. You knew him?
And over in Mandeville, we used to play on. We used to go over there and play on Saturday night, Friday and Saturday.
Buddy wasn't over there. Buddy Petit wasn't over there then, much. No. Bunk over there then, in Mandeville? Did you see Bunk over there?
I didn't see him over there. He was around the house. Yeah.
I know he went over there because he taught Tommy Ladner over there.
He used to play. He used to play with the Superior Baron. Bunk hit.
Did you know a clarinet player from Bay St. Louis named Sumner Labatt? Remember him? Kind of straight clarinet player.
Sumner Labatt?

Yeah, Sumner Labatt. You probably wouldn't remember him, but he's still over there last I heard. He said, say he sounded sort of like Mealy Barnes, if you remember Mealy Barnes. Used to be with Chris Kelly and those guys. Well, anyway. He just used to go out on tours around then on the weekends.
Yeah. Well, we used to go up and down the river. We used to go out to our his hometown and play. You know, up on paydays, you know.
Mm-hmm.

Go across the river. Lake Charles. We'd go. Shreveport. Lefayette. We'd go over in a... Since you're to a... I don't know what town we should go to. We'd go over... We'd go over in a little country town.
Did you ever go over around Alabama, Mobile, any place?
No, I didn't go around there.
You didn't go over towards that?
No.
Those Easterners.
I didn't go there.
